title: Solana PDA Bump and ATA Audit
description: Audit a claimed program-derived-address tuple: paste the program id, seeds with declared encodings (utf8 or hex), the bump seed and the claimed address. The node recomputes the address the runtime rules yield for that exact bump, tests whether the derived bytes land on the Ed25519 curve, scans the canonical bump space 255 down to 1, and reports claimed-matches and bump-canonicality booleans. A second valid address at a non-canonical bump is the substitution class exposed as a fact. Optionally paste wallet, mint and token program for the associated token account under the declared program and the classic Token program side by side. Values only; nothing on-chain is read.

program_id.description: The claimed owning program address, base58 (decodes to 32 bytes). The PDA hash mixes these bytes after the seeds and bump.

seeds.description: Declared seeds in derivation order, each { data, encoding } with encoding "utf8" or "hex". An empty array is valid.

bump.description: The claimed bump seed, one byte. The canonical scan searches 255 down to 1; a claimed bump of 0 is auditable but never canonical.

claimed_address.description: The address the caller believes the tuple yields, base58. Compared by string equality against the recomputation.

wallet.description: Optional ATA mode: wallet address, base58. Requires mint and token_program_id alongside.

mint.description: Optional ATA mode: the mint address, base58.

token_program_id.description: Optional ATA mode: the token program the mint lives under, base58 (Token-2022 or the classic Token program).

mcp_tool_definition.name: audit_solana_pda_ata
mcp_tool_definition.description: Audit a claimed Solana program-derived-address tuple (program id, seeds, bump, claimed address): recomputed address for the claimed bump, on-curve fact, canonical bump and address over the 255-to-1 scan, claimed-matches and bump-canonicality booleans, seed limit facts, and optional side-by-side associated-token-account derivation under a declared token program versus the classic Token program (the Token-2022 wrong-derivation class). Values only; no RPC, no network, no on-chain read.

input_schema_provenance: Top-level properties are exactly the policy_parameters members the kernel reads: program_id, seeds, bump, claimed_address, wallet, mint, token_program_id.
author: PostOakLabs

output_example.note: Derivation per the pinned Solana sources: SHA-256 over seeds (declared order) then the bump byte then the program id then the bytes "ProgramDerivedAddress"; a result that decompresses to an Ed25519 curve point can never be a program-derived address, reported as on_curve. The canonical bump scan follows the pinned client implementation: candidate bumps run 255 down to 1 and the first off-curve result wins, so bump 0 is outside the search space and a claimed bump of 0 is non-canonical even when its recomputed address matches. Limits: at most 16 seeds including the bump seed, each seed at most 32 bytes, restated as facts. ATA derivation uses seeds [wallet, token program id, mint] under program ATokenGPvbdGVxr1b2hvZbsiqW5xWH25efTNsLJA8knL; token_program_mismatch is true exactly when the mint is declared under Token-2022 and the two addresses differ. All comparisons are string equality on pasted values; this kernel reads nothing on-chain.
